key_insight: An adult-trained kidney MRI segmentation model showed promising transfer to pediatric Wilms tumors, but non-inferiority to a pediatric-specific model was not demonstrated.
clinical_relevance: Adult MRI data may help support pediatric tumor segmentation research, though the findings underscore the value of pediatric training data rather than establish clinical readiness.
method: Trained a segmentation model on single-sequence T1- or T2-weighted adult kidney MRI.
Tested on held-out adult data and a pediatric Wilms tumor cohort against a pediatric-specific nnU-Net.
Evaluated Dice similarity coefficient and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance.
evidence_signal: Median lesion Dice scores were 0.86 on adult test data and 0.85 on pediatric data, versus 0.90 for the pediatric-specific model.
watch_item: Cross-domain non-inferiority was not established; pediatric fine-tuning remains a proposed strategy, not a demonstrated improvement.
paper_title: From Adult Renal Masses to Pediatric Wilms Tumors: Evaluating Cross-Domain Generalization of Kidney Lesion Segmentation on MRI
